title: AKS 1.34 cluster is scheduled to leave its 12-month support window
summary: AKS supports a generally available Kubernetes version for 12 months. The supported-versions page gives AKS 1.34 an end of life of 2026-11-30, with long-term support, which must be enabled for the cluster, ending on 2027-11-30.

sources.title: Supported Kubernetes versions in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

constraints: AKS upgrades one minor version at a time and upgrades the control plane before the agent pools.
Long-term support is opt-in per cluster; without it, a version stops receiving patches at the end of its 12-month support window.
An agent pool cannot run a newer version than its control plane, so raise the control plane and the pools together.

steps.title: Raise the cluster version
steps.instructions: Run az aks upgrade with the version in the replacement to move the control plane, after checking the upgrade notes for every minor version crossed.

steps.title: Raise the agent pools
steps.instructions: Run az aks nodepool upgrade for each agent pool so every pool reports the new orchestrator version.

steps.title: Align the cluster declaration
steps.instructions: Set kubernetes_version and each node pool orchestrator_version in the Terraform, Bicep, or Azure Resource Manager definition of the cluster to the same replacement version.

steps.title: Remove APIs the new version deleted
steps.instructions: Read the Kubernetes deprecation guide for every minor version crossed and replace removed API versions in manifests and Helm charts before applying.

verification.purpose: Confirm the API server and kubectl agree on the new version.
Confirm every node runs a compatible version.
